biography.plain_text: King Khalid bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was Saudi Arabia's fourth monarch, ruling from 1975 until his death in 1982. A son of founding king Abdulaziz, he served as governor, interior minister and crown prince before succeeding his brother Faisal. His early preparation combined regional administration, national office and years beside Faisal in the royal succession.

long_biography.plain_text:
Negotiating the Treaty of Taif in 1934 gave future Saudi king Khalid bin Abdulaziz Al Saud an early diplomatic responsibility during the kingdom's formation. He led the Saudi delegation in talks with Yemen, producing the agreement that ended their war and fixed a framework for relations between the neighbours.

Khalid's seven-year reign extended public institutions across education, healthcare and transport. The Ministry of Higher Education was created, medical colleges opened and port administration was consolidated, while Saudi Arabia joined its neighbours in establishing the Gulf Cooperation Council. He also convened the Third Islamic Summit in Makkah. Khalid died in Taif in June 1982 and was succeeded by Fahd.
